name: Gulabsingh Johrimal
summary: One of India's oldest surviving perfumeries, in Dariba Kalan, Old Delhi, founded in 1816 and still run by the founding family.
history:
Lala Gulab Singh moved to Delhi from Jhajjar, in present-day Haryana, and in 1816 set up a perfumery in Old Delhi with his son, Lala Johrimal. The shop, once known locally as 'Gulab Gundhi ki Dukaan' (the shop of Gulab the perfumer), began mainly as an attar-making business. Its head office is still in Dariba Kalan, off Chandni Chowk.

The house describes itself as now run by the seventh and eighth generations of the family.

name: Ajmal Perfumes
summary: Perfume house founded in 1951 in Hojai, Assam, by Haji Ajmal Ali, who started out trading agarwood.
history:
Haji Ajmal Ali was born in 1923 in Alinagar, near Hojai in Assam, to a family of rice farmers. He began by collecting agarwood in the forests of Assam and selling it to dealers, and in 1951 he founded Ajmal Perfumes.

In the early 1960s he moved to Mumbai, where he experimented with perfume blends that were not based on oud. From the late 1960s he travelled around the Gulf, which became one of the business's largest markets.

name: M.L. Ramnarain Perfumers
summary: Kannauj perfumer, established in 1970, that makes natural attars and still runs a traditional distillery in the town.
history: M.L. Ramnarain Perfumers was founded in 1970 by Shri Harinarain Kapoor, from a family with a tradition of making perfumes. National Geographic describes the Ramnarain Perfumers factory as one of the traditional distillers still working in Kannauj.

name: Nizam Attar
summary: A small family attar shop near Charminar, Hyderabad, that traces its business to 1840 and to the Nizams' court.
history:
The business was started by Ghulam Mohammad Ramzan, who came from Kannauj in the mid-1800s to serve the Nizams of Hyderabad, and the shop dates its trade to 1840. Its best-known patron was Mahboob Ali Khan, the sixth Nizam, for whom the founder created a special blend.

The shop, about 80 square feet near Charminar, is run by the fifth generation of the family and stocks around 150 varieties of attar.
